chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn Qurt, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever claims that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, commands immorality and indecency has attributed a lie to Allah. And whoever claims that good and evil take place without the will of Allah, has removed Allah from His Rule. Whoever claims that sins can take place without the power of Allah, has attributed a lie to Allah. And whoever attributes lie to Allah, Allah will cast him into Hell.
He means by good and evil: health and illness, referring to His saying, the Majestic and Glorious: 'And We try you by evil and good by way of probation.'
And We try you by evil and good by way of probation.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God commanding evil and God willing evil in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* refutes the extremes of *Jabriyya* (absolute determinism) and *Mu'tazila* (relinquishment) by establishing a nuanced Shia view of *qadr*. It clarifies that while God’s will encompasses all existence, including health and illness, He commands moral good and permits evil through His power without being the direct author of sin. The interpretation of 'good and evil' as health and illness aligns with the concept of *fitna* (trial), emphasizing human agency within divine sovereignty.
